rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mixing one thing into another does not entail reciprocal mixing; the objection conflates mixing with mutual intermixture.
rows.anchor: والحق أن إختلاط أحد الشيئين بالآخر مستلزم لإختلاط الآخر به وأما خلط أحدهما بالآخر فلا يستلزم خلط الآخر به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi favors al-Sakkaki's two sequences of good then bad and bad then good over al-Zamakhshari's apparent identity of the acts, but rejects annulment as Mu'tazilite.
rows.anchor: وكلام الزمخشري ظاهر في إتحادهما وفيه مافيه ولذلك رجح ما ذهب إليه السكاكي لكن ماذكره من الإحباط ميل إلى مذهب المعتزلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some posit an omitted reciprocal construction, but Alusi calls that ellipsis contrary to the apparent wording.
rows.anchor: نوع من البديع يسمى الإحتباك والأصل خلطوا عملا صالحا بآخر سيء

rows.speaker: ابن المنير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Munir takes mixing to imply doing, as if the verse said they did good and bad deeds, with the preposition omitted.
rows.anchor: واستظهر ابن المنير كون الخلط مضمنا معنى العمل والعدول عن الباء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi takes mixing as bringing together; in context, the good is admitting sins for missing the expedition, and the bad is those sins, with confession foremost.
rows.anchor: وأنا أختار أن الخلط بمعنى الجميع هنا وإذا إعتبر السياق وسبب النزول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Without relying on the occasion, good may be confession of sins generally and bad the sins themselves, or good and bad deeds generally, with good foregrounded as opening reform.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن يراد من العمل الصالح الإعتراف بالذنوب مطلقا ومن السيء الذنوب كذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A saying cited urges following a bad deed with a good one, which erases it; no authority is named.
rows.anchor: ففي الخبر أتبع السيئة بالحسنة تمحها

rows.speaker: الأسود بن قيس
rows.claim: Ibn Sa'd reports Aswad ibn Qays's account of Hasan ibn Ali telling Habib ibn Maslama that serving Mu'awiya for worldly gain damaged his religion.
rows.anchor: وأخرج ابن سعد عن الأسود بن قيس قال : لقي الحسن بن علي رضي الله تعالى عنهما

rows.speaker: مطرف
rows.claim: Matruf compares himself with worshippers of Paradise and people destined for Saqar, then hopes he and his listeners belong among those who confessed sins.
rows.anchor: عن مطرف قال : إني لأستلقي من الليل

rows.speaker: أبو عثمان النهدي
rows.claim: Abu Uthman al-Nahdi says no Qur'anic verse gives him more hope for this community than this one.
rows.anchor: عن أبي عثمان النهدي قال : مافي القرآن آية أرجى عندي لهذه الأمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi reads the hopeful reports as resting on God's promised acceptance, not necessarily prior repentance; he considers 39:53 still more hopeful.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أنه لم يفهم منها صدور التوبة من هؤلاء الآخرين بل ثبت لهم الحكم المفهوم

rows.speaker: غير واحد
rows.claim: Several interpreters infer repentance from confession because the two are customarily associated.
rows.anchor: وجعل غير واحد الإعتراف دالا على التوبة ولعل ذلك لما بينهما من اللزوم عرفا

rows.speaker: الشهاب
rows.claim: Al-Shihab says confession counts as repentance when joined to regret and resolve not to repeat the sin.
rows.anchor: وقال الشهاب : لأنه توبة إذا إقترن بالندم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi objects that general wording cannot imply this particular condition by any of the three recognized modes of indication.
rows.anchor: وقد ذكر أن العام لا يدل على الخاص بإحدى الدلالات الثلاث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although asa ordinarily expresses hope, from the Most Generous it amounts to a promise and certain acceptance of repentance.
rows.anchor: عسى للأطماع وهو من أكرم الأكرمين إيجاب وأي إيجاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's abundant forgiveness and mercy explain acceptance of the penitent as gracious commitment, not an obligation imposed on God as the Mu'tazilites maintain.
rows.anchor: تعليل لما أفادته من وجوب القبول وليس هو الوجوب الذي يقوله المعتزلة

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj identifies the coming day as the appointed day postponed until its term ends; another view refers the pronoun to recompense and stresses divine coming.
rows.anchor: وهو المروي عن ابن جريج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The objection that the day comes on the day of its coming is answered by treating a recurring significant time as an event distinct from the time in which it occurs.
rows.anchor: وأجيب أن كل زمان له شأن يعتبر تجدده كالعيد والنيروز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two grammarians and Nafi retain yāʾ in connected reading but drop it at pause; Ibn Kathir retains it in both, while the other seven drop it in both. Alusi prefers retention in both.
rows.anchor: وقرأ النحويان ونافع ( يأتي ) بإثبات الياء وصلا وحذفها وقفا وابن كثير

rows.speaker: الأعمش
rows.claim: Al-A'mash reads a plural verb, as in Abd Allah's codex, meaning the people or those gathered at the standing-place arrive.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش يوم يأتون بواو الجمع وكذا في مصحف عبدالله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The denied speech is speech that can benefit or save them, such as an answer or intercession, rather than every utterance.
rows.anchor: أي لا تتكلم بما ينفع وينجي من جواب أو شفاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The speech clause most likely governs the preceding temporal adverb; alternatives attach it to the deadline or supply a deleted command to remember.
rows.anchor: وهذا الفعل على الأظهر هو الناصب للظرف السابق

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan is reported to distinguish Judgment Day situations in which speech is forbidden from those in which permission is given.
rows.anchor: وروي هذا عن الحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Permission concerns truthful answers, while false excuses may be allowed to expose their falsity, as in the unbelievers' denial of associating partners with God.
rows.anchor: وقد ذكر غير واحد أن المأذون فيه الأجوبة الحقة والممنوع منه الأعذار الباطلة

rows.speaker: السيد المرتضى
rows.claim: Al-Murtada notes the apparent tension with verses saying people do not speak or receive permission to excuse themselves, and with their questioning one another.
rows.anchor: وفي الدرر والغرر للسيد المرتضى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: False utterances may be permitted to expose unbelievers' claims, such as their denial that they associated partners with God.
rows.anchor: والله ربنا وما كنا مشركين

rows.speaker: قوم من المفسرين
rows.claim: Some commentators reconcile the passages by saying the extended Judgment Day includes periods when speech is forbidden and others when it is permitted.
rows.anchor: وأجاب قوم من المفسرين عن ذلك بأن يوم القيامة يوم طويل ممتد

rows.speaker: السيد المرتضى
rows.claim: Al-Murtada understands denied speech as speech that is heard, accepted, and useful for proof or escape; mere blame and questioning do not count.
rows.anchor: والجواب السديد عن ذلك أن يقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A poet's image of being deaf to a neighbor's speech illustrates how denial can mean denying effective speech, not every sound.
rows.anchor: ومثله قول الشاعر : أعمى إذا ما جارتي خرجت

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: One explanation says they are not ordered to make excuses because that scene has no legal responsibility and terror forces confession.
rows.anchor: إنهم غير مأمورين بالإعتذار فكيف يعتذرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi prefers taking permission to mean their excuses will not be heard or accepted.
rows.anchor: وأحسن من هذا أن يحمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi defends the long-day reconciliation: an extended time can include opposite states that need not last its full duration, and al-Hasan's report can distinguish locations.
rows.anchor: لظهور صحة وقوع الزمان الممتد ظرفا للنقيضين فما إذا لم يقتض كل منهما

rows.speaker: بعض الفضلاء
rows.claim: A scholar says the clause describes a particular moment when the day arrives, so it does not deny speech at other times.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض الفضلاء : لا منافاة بين هذه الآية والآيات التي تدل

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya offers that other dialogue occurred by permission or that speech here means intercession and proof; Alusi dismisses both proposals.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطية : لا بد من أحد أمرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception may be connected to all possible causes of speech or disconnected with an understood reference to speaking by one's own power.
rows.anchor: والإستثناء قيل : من أعم الأسباب أي لا تكلم نفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: 'Among them' refers to those at Judgment's stations, everyone implicit in the generic 'soul,' or the gathered people; a report restricting them to Muhammad's community is very strange.
rows.anchor: فمنهم أي أهل المواقف المدلول عليه بقوله سبحانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase has an omitted repeated 'among them' before 'fortunate,' supplied from the first phrase; the prepositional phrase is fronted and 'wretched' is subject.
rows.anchor: بتقدير ومنهم سعيد وحذف منهم لدلالة الأول عليه

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib defines felicity as divine aid enabling a person to attain good, with wretchedness as its opposite.
rows.anchor: معاونة الأمور الآلهية للإنسان على نيل الخير ويضادها الشقاوة

rows.speaker: البحر
rows.claim: Al-Bahr explains wretchedness as hardship and misery of life, and felicity as its opposite; al-Qamus gives a similar definition.
rows.anchor: وفسر في البحر الشقاوة بنكد العيش و سوئه

rows.speaker: غير واحد
rows.claim: In religious usage, the wretched are those deserving Hell under the threat, and the felicitous those deserving Paradise under the promise.
rows.anchor: وفسر غير واحد الأول بمن إستحق النار بمقتضى الوعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wretched are mentioned first because the passage warns and cautions its audience.
rows.anchor: وتقديم الشقي على السعيد لأن المقام مقام الإنذار والتحذير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those described as wretched are people for whom wretchedness has already been decreed, and they are settled in Hell.
rows.anchor: فأما الذين شقوا ( أي سبقت لهم الشقاوة

rows.speaker: أهل اللغة من الكوفية والبصرية
rows.claim: Kufan and Basran linguists compare zafir to the beginning of a donkey's bray and shahik to its final sound.
rows.anchor: قال أهل اللغة من الكوفية والبصرية : الزفير بمنزلة ابتداء صوت الحمار

rows.speaker: رؤبة
rows.claim: Ru'ba's line describes a sound rising in the chest and a neigh or bray, illustrating the sound terms.
rows.anchor: قال رؤبة : حشرج في الصدر صهيلا أو شهق

rows.speaker: ابن فارس
rows.claim: Ibn Faris defines zafir as exhaling breath and shahik as drawing it back in.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن فارس : الزفير إخراج النفس والشهيق رده

rows.speaker: الشماخ
rows.claim: Al-Shammakh's line about a wild donkey illustrates zafir followed by shahik.
rows.anchor: قال الشماخ في حمار وحش : بعيد مدى التطريب أو صوته زفير

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib says zafir is repeated labored breathing that expands the ribs, related to carrying a heavy load; shahik is prolonged breath and its return.
rows.anchor: وقال الراغب : الزفير ترديد النفس حتى تنتفخ الضلوع

rows.speaker: السائب
rows.claim: Al-Sa'ib unusually assigns zafir to donkeys and shahik to mules.
rows.anchor: وعن السائب أن الزفير للحمير والشهيق للبغال وهو غريب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sounds convey anguish and grief, either picturing people overcome by heat and constricted breath or comparing their voices to donkeys.
rows.anchor: ويراد بهما الدلالة على كربهم وغمهم وتشبيه حالهم بحال من استولت على قلبه الحرارة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the sounds as regret, loud breathing, and uninterrupted weeping.
rows.anchor: والمأثور عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما أنه قال : يريد ندامة ونفسا عاليا

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan reads the verb with a damma on shin, using it transitively as in 'God made him wretched.'
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن ( شقوا ) بضم الشين فاستعمل متعديا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sounds clause is either a fresh sentence answering an implied question about their condition or a circumstantial clause attached to Hell or its pronoun.
rows.anchor: وجملة ( لهم فيها زفير ) إلخ مستأنفة كأن سائلا قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unlike the Hell passage, this verse does not mention the saved people's joy because the treatment of Hell serves warning and admonition.
rows.anchor: لم يذكر ها هنا أن لهم بهجة وسرورا كما ذكر في أهل النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hamza, al-Kisai, Hafs, and several early authorities read the verb passively; most of the seven readers use the active voice.
rows.anchor: قرءاة حمزة والكسائي وحفص ونسبت إلى ابن مسعود وطلحة بن مصرف

rows.speaker: علي بن سليمان
rows.claim: Ali ibn Sulayman preferred the active reading and wondered how al-Kisai could read the passive despite his Arabic expertise.
rows.anchor: وكان يقول عجبا من الكسائي كيف قرأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi rejects the criticism of al-Kisai: his reading is transmitted authentically, not based on opinion, and is not unique.
rows.anchor: ولم يقرأ بالرأي ولم يتفرد بذلك

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra' says Hudhayl uses sa'adahu Allah with the meaning of as'adahu, supporting the transitive passive reading.
rows.anchor: وذكر أن الفراء حكى أن هذيلا تقول سعده الله تعالى

rows.speaker: الجوهري
rows.claim: Al-Jawhari gives the active pattern sa'ida, fa-huwa sa'id, and the passive description mas'ud.
rows.anchor: وقال الجوهري سعد بالكسرة فهو سعيد مثل قولهم سلم فهو سليم وسعد فهو مسعود

rows.speaker: القشيري
rows.claim: Al-Qushayri distinguishes sa'adahu Allah as mas'ud from as'adahu Allah as mus'ad.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو نصر عبد الرحيم القشيري ورد سعده الله تعالى فهو مسعود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The contrast between active 'they were wretched' and passive 'they were made felicitous' intimates that granted felicity merits gratitude to God.
rows.anchor: وما ألطف الإشارة في - شقوا وسعدوا - على قراءة البناء للفاعل في الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gift is not cut off or terminated; Ibn Qutayba notes forms with dhal or dal, with dhal more common.
rows.anchor: أي غير مقطوع عنهم ولا مخترم ومصدره الجذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi prefers parsing 'gift' as a cognate accusative implied by being in Paradise and remaining there; alternatives make it a state or specification of divine willing.
rows.anchor: ونصب عطاءا على المصدرية من معنى الجملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other parses treat 'gift' as a state of an implied object of willing or a specification clarifying whether the gift can be cut off.
rows.anchor: وقيل هو نصب على الحالية من المفعول المقدر للمشيئة أو تمييز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the reward an unbroken gift emphasizes permanence and blocks the inference that the exception entails Paradise's end.
rows.anchor: مبالغة في التأبيد ودفعا لما يتوهم من ظاهر الاستثناء من الانقطاع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation says the gift clause assures that the reward itself never ends, so the exception denotes successive blessings and God's pleasure, or a limitation at the beginning.
rows.anchor: وقيل إن ذلك لبيان أن ثواب أهل الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Hell passage ends by saying God does as He wills, signaling that He may relieve some and leave others; Paradise instead closes with unending grace.
rows.anchor: ولهذا فرق في النظم بين التأبيد من حيث تمم الأول

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Ibn al-Mundhir transmits al-Hasan's report that even if Hell's people remained as long as the sands of Alij, they would have a day when they leave.
rows.anchor: بما أخرجه ابن المنذر عن الحسن قال قال عمر لو لبث أهل النار

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Ishaq ibn Rahawayh transmits Abu Hurayra's report that a day will come when no one remains in Hell.
rows.anchor: إسحاق بن راهويه عن أبي هريرة قال سيأتي على جهنم

rows.speaker: إبراهيم
rows.claim: Ibn al-Mundhir and Abu al-Shaykh transmit Ibrahim's view that this is the Qur'an's most hopeful verse for Hell's inhabitants.
rows.anchor: وأخرج ابن المنذر وأبو الشيخ عن إبراهيم قال ما في القرآن آية أرجى لأهل النار

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Mas'ud predicts a time when Hell's doors will clap shut.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن مسعود ليأتين عليها زمان تصفق فيه أبوابها

rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: Al-Tabari transmits al-Sha'bi's saying that Hell is the faster of the two abodes to fill and the faster to decay.
rows.anchor: وأخرج ابن جرير عن الشعبي قال جهنم أسرع الدارين عمرانا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi affirms the consensus that unbelievers remain eternally in Hell; decisive proofs outweigh reports of its emptying, the verse does not prove the contrary, and abrogation is unnecessary.
rows.anchor: وانت تعلم أن خلود الكفار مما أجمع عليه المسلمين ولا عبرة بالمخالف

rows.speaker: ابن الجوزي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Jawzi declared some reports fabricated, including the claim that Hell will empty of Adam's descendants and its doors clap like monotheists' houses.
rows.anchor: وقد نص ابن الجوزي على وضع بعضها كخبر عن عبد الله بن عمرو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports about Hell emptying do not overcome decisive evidence for unbelievers' eternal punishment; there is no need to claim this verse was abrogated.
rows.anchor: ولا يقاوم واحدا منها كثير من هذه الأخبار ولا دليل في الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sequence gathers all souls, divides them into wretched and fortunate, then partitions the groups; al-Sharif al-Qayrawani's poem illustrates the pattern.
rows.anchor: وقد ذكر أن في الآية صيغة الجمع مع التفريق والتقسيم أما الجمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi cites the verse's general statement about every soul and the following division as a progression from gathering to classification.
rows.anchor: في الآية صيغة الجمع مع التفريق والتقسيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The successive fa particles continue the sequence, and the wording intimates that wretchedness and felicity were settled beforehand.
rows.anchor: ومن هنا يعلم حال الفاءين فاء فمنهم وفاء فأما

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ahmad, al-Tirmidhi, and al-Nasa'i report Ibn Umar's account of the Prophet showing two complete, unalterable books listing Paradise and Hell's people; each person's end matches their deeds, so servants should act steadily.
rows.anchor: خرج علينا رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم وفي يده كتابان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report that a person's wretchedness or felicity is set in the womb is explained as the angel learning the decree or, interpretively, as disclosure of God's prior knowledge.
rows.anchor: وجاء في حديث الشقي من شقي في بطن أمه والسعيد من سعد في بطن أمه

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: Al-Tirmidhi grades hasan a report from Umar: the decree is finished and written, yet each person is made easy for what they were created.
rows.anchor: عن عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله تعالى عنه قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The past tense expresses certainty; singular forms portray each party as a unit before plural wording reflects entry into the two abodes in successive groups.
rows.anchor: عبر بالماضي إشارة إلى تحقق الوقوع وأتى بالموصول جمعا إيذانا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening is an exhortation carrying figurative lament: why were there not people in earlier communities to resist corruption?
rows.anchor: فلولا كان ( تحضيض فيه معنى التفجع مجازا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baqiyya can mean a surviving quality of judgment and reason or excellence; metaphorically it is what one selects and stores for benefit, hence one of the best people.
rows.anchor: أي ذوو خصلة باقية من الرأي والعقل أو ذوو فضل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another possibility is baqiyya as baqwa, self-preservation: people protecting themselves from what brings God's anger and punishment.
rows.anchor: وجوز أن تكون البقية بمعنى البقوى كالتقية بمعنى التقوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading pronounces baqiyya on the measure of a single instance from baqahu, 'to wait for or watch'; it asks why people were not vigilant in fear of punishment.
rows.anchor: بزنة المرة وهو مصدر بقاه يبقيه كرماه يرميه

rows.speaker: معاذ بن جبل
rows.claim: In a report about the delayed night prayer, Mu'adh says they waited for the Messenger of God; this usage illustrates baqina as waiting.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث عن معاذ بن جبل قال : بقينا رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading lightens the yāʾ and treats baqiya as a feminine active participle, like shajiyat.
rows.anchor: وقريء ( بقية ) بتخفيف الياء إسم فاعل من بقي
